findings.title: The mpd_worktree_create tool description does not name the short-name-only rule
evidence: The description now names the protected-branch refusal but not the new `refs/...` invalid-branch refusal.
The refusal message itself names the accepted short form, and all four docs carry the rule, so no caller is left without a remedy.
findings.why_it_matters: The tool schema is the only text a calling model sees before its first attempt; without the clause the rule is learned only by a refusal. Documentation-only consistency, not a behaviour defect.
findings.fix_direction: Add one clause to the create tool description (a SHORT branch name is required; a `refs/...` spelling is refused with invalid-branch). No behaviour change; no gate re-run beyond the normal set is implied.

out_of_scope_observations: packages/mpd-worktree-plugin/src/git.ts -> headOf (the MAIN checkout) still uses `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`; a tag sharing the main branch's name makes head.ref `heads/<name>`, which still resolves for base/merge/ancestry but does not match the exact-string merge-target protectedBranches check in mergeWorktree. This is pre-existing at HEAD (the protected-target check exists there and headOf is unchanged by this diff) and was disclosed by the writer; it is NOT introduced or fixed by this repair. One-line report per the bounded scope; schedule separately if the captain wants it.
declined_to_judge: Protection added to the config AFTER a record exists deliberately freezes remove/merge (the revalidation is force-blind by design) — intentional operator-owned behaviour.
protectedBranches entries are not trimmed in resolveConfig, so a config value with spaces protects nothing — pre-existing config behaviour untouched by this diff.

A legal branch literally named `<something>/refs/...` is not refused, and a branch literally named `refs/<x>` IS refused although it round-trips — the latter is exactly the frozen F2 wording ('any refs/-rooted branch'), so accepted as requirement, not a defect.
A config branchPrefix of `refs/...` now makes member creation degrade to undefined with ONE log line (D4) instead of creating a nested ref — intended under the short-name rule.
Case-insensitive filesystems and Windows path handling were not exercised (Linux only).
Ref classes other than tags (remote-tracking refs, notes) shadowing a branch name were not enumerated; `symbolic-ref` covers the class by construction and the tag cases were proven end-to-end.

Every pre-existing test assertion was not re-read line-by-line; the full suite was executed and the test inventory checked for removed/weakened arms (none: only the import line changed in existing content).

The writer's reverted-source falsification logs were not replayed; instead the pre-fix premises were established directly (heads/feature abbreviation; check-ref-format admitting refs/heads/dev and the nested ref being created).
